title: Release plan: enable mixed-workload scheduler prototype in us-east canary
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Enable the mixed-workload scheduler prototype (short/long prompt-aware two-queue policy) in a limited production canary in us-east, with clear ramp steps, monitoring/rollback criteria, and a decision checkpoint to either expand, iterate, or roll back.

Context
We’ve seen user-visible p95 tail latency spikes under mixed prompt-length distributions (short chat prompts interleaved with long-context prompts) due to head-of-line blocking during long prefill and batch selection. The prototype biases dispatch toward latency-sensitive short prompts while guaranteeing progress for long prompts via aging/starvation prevention + token budget guardrails.

Canary scope
1) Hosted API (us-east)
- Region: us-east
- Target: a single canary pool (hosted) with low blast radius and good baseline traffic diversity.
- Proposed pool(s) (final names to confirm with SRE inventory):
  - hosted-us-east-canary-a (primary)
  - hosted-us-east-canary-b (backup / rollback landing)
- Traffic allocation: start at 1% of hosted-us-east traffic (routing policy: canary header override + default random sample).

2) Dedicated (us-east)
- Target: one dedicated pool with internal-friendly customer(s) and flexible comms.
- Proposed pool(s):
  - dedicated-us-east-canary-1 (primary)
- Traffic allocation: enable only for selected model routes (e.g., top 1–2 chat models) to limit variability.

Feature flag + config strategy
Flag
- runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled (default: false)
- runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.mode = {"off" | "observe" | "enforce"}
  - observe: classification + metrics only; no dispatch bias
  - enforce: full two-queue dispatch + token budgets + aging

Config knobs (initial canary defaults; tuned per SKU where applicable)
- short_classification_threshold_tokens: 256 (subject to trace sensitivity results)
- long_classification_threshold_tokens: 1024 (used only for debug labeling; classification is binary)
- short_queue_target_share: 0.70
- long_queue_min_share: 0.20 (guardrail; ensures progress under sustained short traffic)
- aging_half_life_ms: 1500
- max_short_burst_ms: 200 (limits starvation risk when short traffic is spiky)
- per_iteration_token_budget_short: 4096
- per_iteration_token_budget_long: 4096
- max_queue_skew: 8x (alerts if dispatch skew exceeds this for >5m)

Rollout note: all knobs must be pool-configurable (Dedicated) and region/pool configurable (Hosted). We should avoid model-specific overrides in the first canary unless we observe clear instability tied to a single model.

Ramp plan (proposed)
Pre-checks (T-2 days)
- Confirm perf-canary green for mixed workloads for runtime-1.18 candidate on representative SKUs (nightly and an on-demand run).
- Confirm dashboards available and alerts routed to #eng-sre and #eng-runtime.
- Confirm rollback path tested in staging: flipping flag + reverting config returns scheduler to baseline and stabilizes queue behavior.

Step 0: Staging burn-in (T-1 day)
- Enable mode=observe in staging for 24h.
- Validate:
  - Classification distribution looks sane (short/long split roughly matches expectations from trace analysis).
  - No unexpected metric/cardinality blow-ups.
  - No scheduler loop regressions or excessive debug logs.

Step 1: Prod canary (Hosted us-east) – observe only (Day 1)
- 1% traffic, mode=observe.
- Validate metrics correctness and baseline comparisons (no behavior change expected).
- Proceed to enforce only if:
  - Metrics stable; no SLO drift beyond noise.
  - No evidence of kernel selection thrash associated with new hooks.

Step 2: Prod canary (Hosted us-east) – enforce (Day 2)
- 1% traffic, mode=enforce.
- Hold for minimum 2 hours; extend to 24h if traffic patterns allow.
- Success criteria (Hosted):
  - p95 TTFT improvement for short-class requests: >= 10% vs baseline pool at similar load, or absolute reduction agreed with PM (Nikhil Sharma).
  - No more than 2% throughput regression (tokens/sec) at pool level, unless explicitly traded for p95 improvement and approved by runtime lead + product.
  - Long-class p95 does not regress beyond guardrails (see rollback criteria below).

Step 3: Increase Hosted canary exposure (Day 3)
- Move to 5% traffic if Step 2 is clean.
- Optional: 10% for a 4–6h window if error budget allows and SRE approves.

Step 4: Dedicated canary enablement (Day 3–4)
- Enable mode=enforce for dedicated-us-east-canary-1 on selected routes.
- Require explicit customer ops acknowledgement if the account is external; otherwise use internal-friendly accounts.
- Success criteria (Dedicated):
  - Reduced p95 completion latency for short prompts under mixed workloads and no sustained long request starvation events.

Monitoring plan (dashboards / metrics)
Primary dashboards (must be open during ramp)
- Scheduler class metrics dashboard (per-class queue depth, time-in-queue, dispatch share)
- Hosted API tail latency SLO dashboard (us-east)
- GPU saturation + batching efficiency (pool-level)

Key metrics to watch
- request_queue_time_ms{class=short|long} p50/p95
- prefill_latency_ms{class=*} p50/p95
- ttft_ms{class=*} p50/p95
- completion_latency_ms{class=*} p50/p95
- starvation_counter_total{class=long}
- dispatch_share{class=short|long}
- token_budget_overrun_total{class=*}
- scheduler_iteration_time_ms p95 (ensure no scheduler overhead regression)

Rollback triggers (align with SRE guardrails)
Immediate rollback (flip enabled=false) if any of the below occur for >10 minutes and correlate to canary pool:
- Hosted us-east p95 (overall) increases beyond allowed drift in SRE guardrails, with canary pool as primary contributor.
- Long-class starvation_counter_total increases steadily (indicates aging/min-share is failing in practice).
- Error rate increase (5xx/429 attributable to queue buildup) beyond guardrail thresholds.
- Kernel selection instability symptoms: rapid oscillation in selected kernels / significant perf jitter tied to mixed batches (as confirmed by runtime on-point).

Soft rollback / parameter adjust (with approval from runtime + SRE) if:
- Long-class latency regresses while short-class improves: consider increasing long_queue_min_share or reducing max_short_burst_ms.
- Throughput regression >2%: consider adjusting per-iteration token budgets or short_queue_target_share.

Comms plan
- #eng-releases: announce schedule, ramp steps, on-point roster, and rollback authority.
- #eng-runtime: live notes during ramp (config diffs, observed metrics, changes made).
- #eng-sre: monitoring responsibility, alert acknowledgements, and incident escalation path.
- If Dedicated external customer involved: CS/Sales notified via internal note with timing and rollback expectations (Lauren Bishop to coordinate with account team).

Decision meeting
Schedule a 30-minute checkpoint after 24h of enforce mode at >=5% Hosted traffic (or earlier if we hit rollback triggers).
Attendees: Connor O’Brien, Lena Fischer, Sofia Ivanova, Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello, Nikhil Sharma, Lauren Bishop, Mateo Alvarez.
Agenda:
- Results summary: p95 deltas (short vs long), throughput, error budget impact.
- Any incidents / near-misses.
- Parameter changes made during canary (and why).
- Decision:
  - Expand canary (more pools / higher %),
  - Hold and iterate (specific follow-up issues), or
  - Roll back and reassess approach.

Checklist (blocking for Step 2 enforce)
- [ ] ENG-2463 SRE guardrails reviewed + explicit approval in ticket comments
- [ ] Dashboard deployed and verified (metric names/labels final; no high-cardinality surprises)
- [ ] Perf-canary green for mixed scenarios on runtime-1.18 candidate
- [ ] Config bounds validated (no unsafe values can be pushed via config service)
- [ ] Runbook finalized with exact flag/config keys and rollback steps

- 2026-02-27 (Rafael Mendes): SRE prefers observe-only for at least 2h in prod before enforce. Requested explicit rollback authority statement: SRE on-point can roll back without waiting for runtime approval if SLO guardrails are violated.

Open questions
- Final selection of canary pools (Hosted and Dedicated) and whether we can ensure comparable baseline pool for A/B.
- Whether to include a long-spike scenario in perf-canary gating for the exact us-east SKU mix before enabling enforce.
- Confirm how we will report results (single doc vs Slack summary + link to benchmark results summary).
